name: Intermediate
title: Independent and Understood
tagline: Share opinions, tell stories and cope confidently with most situations.
overview: B1 is the independence level. You stop translating every sentence and start linking ideas: relative clauses, connectors, the passive and polite Konjunktiv II. The course adds formal writing and workplace and university communication, so your German works outside the classroom.
levelGoal: By the end of B1 you can explain and defend an opinion, write a formal email, understand the main points of authentic texts, and deal with unexpected everyday problems.
canDo: Express and justify opinions on familiar topics.
Write formal and semi-formal emails and letters.
Follow the main points of clear standard German.
Describe experiences and solve problems in everyday situations.

modules.title: Opinions & Connections
modules.summary: Politeness, contrast and cause: the language of a thoughtful conversation.

lessons.title: Konjunktiv II for Polite Requests
lessons.summary: Sound considerate rather than demanding with könnte, würde and hätte.
objectives: Form the most common Konjunktiv II verbs.
Ask for help, permission and favours politely.
Recognise unreal wishes and hypothetical situations.

lessons.title: Connectors & Word Order
lessons.summary: Link ideas with deshalb, trotzdem and außerdem — and keep the verb in the right place.
objectives: Use deshalb, darum and deswegen to express consequence.
Contrast ideas with aber, trotzdem and allerdings.
Apply correct word order after coordinating and subordinating connectors.

keyPhrase.de: Es regnet, trotzdem gehe ich spazieren.
keyPhrase.en: It is raining; nevertheless, I am going for a walk.

lessons.title: Expressing & Justifying Opinions
lessons.summary: Agree, disagree and explain why without sounding blunt.
objectives: Introduce opinions with meiner Meinung nach and ich finde, dass.
Give balanced agreement and disagreement.
Support an opinion with reasons and examples.

keyPhrase.de: Meiner Meinung nach sollte man mehr Rad fahren.
keyPhrase.en: In my opinion, people should cycle more.

modules.title: Complex Sentences
modules.summary: Relative clauses, zu-infinitives and verb-preposition combinations.

lessons.title: Relative Clauses
lessons.summary: Add detail to a noun with der, die, das and the right case.
objectives: Choose relative pronouns by gender, number and case.
Place the conjugated verb at the end of the clause.
Combine two sentences into one fluent relative sentence.

keyPhrase.de: Das ist der Kollege, der mir geholfen hat.
keyPhrase.en: That is the colleague who helped me.

lessons.title: Infinitive Clauses with zu
lessons.summary: Express intentions, plans and obligations with zu + infinitive and um … zu.
objectives: Use zu + infinitive after verbs such as vorhaben and vergessen.
Express purpose with um … zu.
Place zu correctly with separable verbs.

keyPhrase.de: Ich habe vor, im Sommer nach Wien zu fahren.
keyPhrase.en: I plan to go to Vienna in the summer.

lessons.title: Verb–Preposition Combinations
lessons.summary: Learn the preposition each verb demands and ask questions with wo- and da-compounds.
objectives: Use high-frequency verb–preposition pairs correctly.
Form questions with worauf, womit and wofür.
Use da-compounds such as darauf and damit.

keyPhrase.de: Ich interessiere mich für deutsche Geschichte.
keyPhrase.en: I am interested in German history.

modules.title: Written German
modules.summary: From a quick message to a formal email — register, structure and the passive.

lessons.title: Formal vs Informal Register
lessons.summary: Choose between du and Sie, and adjust tone for work, officials and friends.
objectives: Select formal or informal address for different relationships.
Use formal request and apology formulas.
Recognise register shifts in authentic emails.

lessons.title: Emails & Letters
lessons.summary: Structure a German email: subject, salutation, request, closing.
objectives: Write an appropriate subject line and salutation.
Make a clear request and provide context.
Close formally and informally with the right formula.

lessons.title: The Passive Voice: An Introduction
lessons.summary: Shift focus from who acts to what happens with werden + past participle.
objectives: Form the present and past passive.
Decide when the passive is more appropriate than the active.
Understand agent phrases with von and durch.

keyPhrase.en: The invoice will be paid tomorrow.

modules.title: Real-World Contexts
modules.summary: University, workplace and the language of sorting things out.

lessons.title: University Communication
lessons.summary: Enrol, ask questions and write to lecturers with confidence.
objectives: Ask about enrolment, deadlines and course requirements.
Write a short, polite email to a lecturer.
Understand common university abbreviations.

keyPhrase.de: Ich würde gern einen Termin mit Ihnen vereinbaren.
keyPhrase.en: I would like to arrange an appointment with you.

lessons.title: Workplace Communication
lessons.summary: Meetings, clarifications and the small talk that keeps work human.
objectives: Contribute to a meeting with clear updates.
Ask for clarification without losing the thread.
Use appropriate small-talk phrases with colleagues.

lessons.title: Solving Everyday Problems
lessons.summary: Complain, explain and negotiate a solution calmly and clearly.
objectives: Describe a problem precisely and politely.
Request a replacement, refund or repair.
Respond to an apology and agree on next steps.

keyPhrase.de: Ich habe ein Problem mit meiner Bestellung.
keyPhrase.en: I have a problem with my order.
